text: You built indexes back in T-SQL Development. This lesson is about what the optimizer actually does with them at runtime -- which shows up in the plan as one of a small set of operators you'll see constantly.

An Index Seek navigates straight to matching rows -- targeted, usually good. An Index Scan reads the entire index top to bottom. A Key Lookup is a second trip back to the clustered index for columns the nonclustered index didn't cover.
Filter on a plain column and you likely get a seek. Wrap that column in a function like YEAR, and the predicate stops being SARGable -- the optimizer can't use an index seek even if one exists.

Nested Loops is cheap when one side is small. Hash Match builds an in-memory hash table and can spill to tempdb. Sort is explicit and often the target for a better index. Compute Scalar evaluates an expression, often right before a Filter.

An Index Seek followed immediately by a Key Lookup on thousands of rows is the single most common index fix in real DBA work. Next up: finding exactly which indexes are missing, duplicated, or dead weight.
